preserved_objections.basis: The proposed mechanism cannot address the core failure mode of moisture and oxygen barrier degradation in ethylene-vinyl alcohol layers, as the nanoparticles would be dispersed within the matrix but not specifically reinforce or protect the barrier layer itself.

The boundary condition requires protection of the ethylene-vinyl alcohol layer during distribution, but the proposed intervention does nothing to prevent humidity plasticization of this specific layer.
Evidence [europepmc:42280608] indicates that active packaging strategies focus on antimicrobial properties rather than barrier enhancement, contradicting the need to address barrier degradation.
The proposed mechanism provides antimicrobial functionality but fails to improve upon the baseline's barrier properties against moisture and oxygen, which is the specific failure being addressed.

Creating core-shell nanoparticles with pH-responsive polymer shells dispersed throughout a multilayer film would disrupt the structural integrity and layer adhesion of the ethylene-vinyl alcohol barrier layer, as evidenced by challenges in [europepmc:33652755] regarding maintaining barrier properties in active packaging systems.

The testable prediction focuses on antimicrobial release kinetics and efficacy, but fails to measure the critical parameter of barrier properties improvement against moisture and oxygen, which is the actual failure mode.
